title: AI Video Extender
summary: Extend a video with AI in Flick: add new footage after or before your clip with Wan 3.0 or Seedance 2.5, on the canvas or by asking the agent.
body_markdown:
### Is there a free AI video extender?


Flick is free to start, with 100 credits at signup and 100 credits every day, no credit card needed. Extend Video runs on the Standard plan ($20 a month), and on the free plan you can extract a clip's last frame and animate it with MiniMax H3 Fast to continue the shot.


### How long can an AI video extension be?


In Flick, Wan 3.0 adds 2 to 30 seconds to a clip of up to 15 seconds, as long as the two together stay within 30 seconds, and Seedance 2.5 adds 4 to 30 seconds to a clip of 2 to 30 seconds. To go longer, extend the extended clip again or add shots in the editor.


### Does an extended video keep the same character and look?


Yes, because the model reads the end of your clip and continues from it. Keep the prompt to the new action, lock the camera and say the character stays in frame; if a take drifts, run it again rather than describing the character a second time.


### Can AI extend a video before it starts?


Yes. Set Extend direction to Before the clip, and the model generates the footage leading into your first frame, which works for a lead in or an establishing moment before the action.


### How many credits does it cost to extend a video?


Wan 3.0 costs 12 credits a second at 720p, the default resolution, counted on your clip plus the new footage, and Seedance 2.5 costs 29 credits a second at 720p for the new footage and your clip. The Standard plan includes 2,500 credits a month.


### Does the AI video extender add sound?


Yes. Both Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5 generate sound with the new footage, and the Generate Audio setting costs the same on or off.


### What is the best AI video extender in Flick?


Wan 3.0 is the default and the one to use for clips of real people, while Seedance 2.5 takes longer source clips, of 2 to 30 seconds. Try both on the same clip on one canvas and keep the take that matches your shot.


### Can I make the extended video sharper?


Yes. Run Upscale Video on the result, with Bytedance Upscale on the Free plan or Topaz Video Upscale on Standard, or ask the agent to upscale it after it extends the clip.
